exposure: clinical indications for hysterectomy (atonic PPH, uterine rupture, placenta accreta spectrum disorders)
outcome: maternal outcomes (postoperative complications, blood transfusion requirements, maternal mortality, sepsis, hemorrhagic shock)
cohort: The study included 110 patients who underwent emergency peripartum hysterectomy after either a vaginal or cesarean delivery.
finding: The frequency of emergency peripartum hysterectomy was 1.8 per 1,000 deliveries, primarily indicated by placenta accreta spectrum disorders, uterine rupture, and atonic postpartum hemorrhage, with a maternal mortality rate of 5.5%.
mod_finding: Emergency peripartum hysterectomy was more commonly linked to cesarean deliveries (72.7%) compared to vaginal births, and abnormal placentation was strongly correlated with prior cesarean sections.
